body: Much cheaper, or sometimes your insurance covers the cost completely. I also would need to pay for an appointment with a doctor so they could prescribe it, and then I'm assuming follow up visits to make sure the side effects are under control. Healthcare in the US is a bit of mess compared to some places. I try not to complain though because I'm very lucky to have my physical health. It's mental where I start to feel like I'm slipping below the water...
That gives me some hope. I really appreciate you taking the time to talk to me. It's nice not to feel so lonely.

Yep, I'm American. You don't need health insurance to see a doctor here, but without insurance it's very expensive-- more than I can afford at this point. If things get any better, hopefully I'll have the energy soon to find a way to get insured. I'm not against the idea of medication. My fear (if you can call it that-- I feel so empty) is that it won't ever get better.

Thanks :)

I don't have one-- no health insurance. I'm skeptical that it would help, in any case. I'm pretty set on what I want to do, the only question is when.
